items.title: Game of Thrones Author George R.R. Martin Shares Personal Update, Discusses Health and 'Falling Further and Further Behind'
items.description: 77-year-old Game of Thrones author George R.R. Martin has shared a candid update on his health, and discussed "falling further and further behind."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
77-year-old Game of Thrones author George R.R. Martin has shared a candid update on his health, and discussed "falling further and further behind."

Penning his first entry in six months on his personal blog, Martin acknowledged the lack of recent updates and described the year so far as having been "stressful, to say the least."

"So much has been happening, it's been overwhelming," Martin wrote in a post titled 'Better Late Than Never.' "Some great things, exciting things. Dreams coming true. But there have been nightmares too. I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression. The worst may be yet to come.

"I turned 77 last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun," Martin continued. "But there have been amazing times as well."

Ending the blog on a more positive note, Martin celebrated the nine Emmy nominations recently secured by Game of Thrones spinoff A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms and said he "will try and catch up some" on posting in future.

No mention was made in the post on what Martin has been working on recently, and there was (perhaps unsurprisingly) also no mention of House of the Dragon, after Martin previously described his working relationship with showrunner Ryan Condal as "abysmal."

Martin has previously discussed losing fellow authors and peers, as well as his friend, Hollywood legend Robert Redford, who came out of retirement last year for a brief cameo with Martin in his AMC series Dark Winds. Speaking earlier this year, Martin also said that if he never completes Game of Thrones sequel Winds of Winter (or the book after that), there's no plan for anyone else to step in. Instead, his Song of Ice and Fire series simply "won't be finished."

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter about his lack of progress on his next novel, Martin said he would "hate" to give up on the series — though admitted he had made little progress in recent years. At the same time, Martin has served as a producer on Game of Thrones' various TV spinoffs and Dark Winds, and continued publishing of various A Song of Ice and Fire companion novels — with at least two new Dunk and Egg adventures also currently left part-finished.

The Game of Thrones franchise shows no sign of slowing down, however, with a new stage play set to begin soon in the U.K., and early plans for a potential HBO Game of Thrones sequel series starring Arya Stark.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Hides a Secret Character Who's Already Appeared in a String of MCU Movies and Could Become the Next Spider Superhero
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day hides an appearance by yet another Marvel Comics superhero — someone who has quietly made cameos in previous Spider-Man and Avengers movies. Did you spot them?
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day hides an appearance by yet another Marvel Comics superhero — someone who has quietly made cameos in previous Spider-Man and Avengers movies. Did you spot them?

In the comics, Cindy Moon is well known via her alter ego Silk, who begins her superhero journey as a Korean-American student bitten by the same spider as Peter Parker. But fewer fans will know that Cindy has also been quietly teased within the MCU for a decade, with appearances in a string of films.

In Brand New Day, Cindy is the student in Bruce Banner's class who asks the question about Thanos — why the big purple baddie didn't just double the universe's resources instead of killing half of its life. It's a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment (and a good question!), but actually the latest in a consistent series of cameos.

Why isn’t anyone talking about this!?!

Cindy Moon was in Dr.Banner’s Class#SpiderManBrandNewDay pic.twitter.com/NBg1eitRxU

— •tr1stan⛷️ (@nuel_irl) July 31, 2026

Cindy first appeared in Spider-Man: Homecoming, portrayed by actress Tiffany Espensen, and makes numerous appearances throughout the movie as one of Peter's classmates. While Cindy largely remains in the background, she still has a few lines of dialogue — enough that her character remains notable enough to appear again in future.

Audiences next glimpsed Cindy in Avengers: Infinity War, on the same school bus as Peter and Ned, again played by Espensen. Fast forward to Spider-Man: No Way Home, and Cindy returns one more time via the film's extended cut post-credit scene that features previously-unused footage.

I’m literally dropping a video later today on this.

They are different actress and the build up story is all over the place for Cindy moon.

And the cancellation of the silk spider society show would have played into the SSU spiderverse Sony is building 🤙 https://t.co/v2WC731d06

— KING SPYKE (@KingSpyke_) August 3, 2026

With Espensen now seemingly retired from acting, Brand New Day sees Shannon Young Cho take on Cindy's role — and continue on the character in Tom Holland's second trilogy of films. But where is this all going? Is Marvel playing the long game with Cindy's introduction, or is this just a fun set of Easter eggs for Cindy Moon fans?

"Seeing the same character in three movies doesn't feel random," one fan wrote wrote on social media. "It looks like Marvel is slowly setting up something bigger."

"Marvel/Sony are definitely slowly soft launching Cindy Moon to the general public more and more and I cannot wait to see Silk," said another.

"Cindy f***ing Moon has more MCU appearances than Shang Chi," noted another fan.

While Cindy's MCU future isn't yet certain, the jaw-dropping success of Brand New Day now makes Spider-Man 5 seem inevitable. Perhaps we'll finally see Silk emerge then?

items.title: 'She Ended on a Really Great Note': Jessica Henwick Says She's Turned Down Returning as Colleen Wing in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3
items.description: Iron Fist star Jessica Henwick has said her character Colleen Wing won't return in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, despite talks with Marvel.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Iron Fist star Jessica Henwick has said her character Colleen Wing won't return in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, despite talks with Marvel.

Wing previously appeared in the Netflix series Iron Fist, Luke Cage and The Defenders, and eventually inherited the Iron Fist mantle from the show's lead character, Danny Rand.

Fans had hoped that Colleen Wing would make her return in the upcoming third season of Daredevil: Born Again, which is expected to reunite the main four Defenders for the first time in almost a decade. However, Henwick has said that while she had discussed returning in the role with Marvel, she ultimately opted to pass on the opportunity.

"I've said multiple times over the years, I would love to come back. I know that everyone is back this season. I'm not in this season," Henwick told Inverse. "We did have discussions about whether I should go back this season. But for me, her story ended with her going off into the sunset. She has the Iron Fist. She's got Misty by her side. Daughters of the Dragon is happening. She ended on a really great note."

Any future storyline involving Colleen needed to be worth "unpicking" that ending, Henwick continued, rather than having her return only to be "just stood in the back of the shot."

"I'm just not interested in bringing her back unless it's worth sort of unpicking that happiness, because obviously she can't be happy on a TV series," Henwick concluded. "If she's back, something's gone wrong. I would absolutely love to come back, but it would just really have to be the right story."

Famously, Henwick previously turned down an appearance as a different character in Marvel movie Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, in the hope that Colleen Wing could still return in future. (This was before Daredevil: Born Again came along and began reviving Marvel's Netflix era in full force.)

It sounds like Henwick is still keen to make a return as Colleen Wing someday, then, but don't expect to see her when Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 debuts in spring 2027. The only question now, however, is whether Daredevil: Born Again will continue on and get a Season 4.

The past week has seen Marvel scrap its planned Season 2 of Emmy-nominated series Wonder Man, leaving the brand's live-action TV future in doubt. Currently, just Daredevil: Born Again and Vision Quest are on Marvel's upcoming TV slate, and both have already finished filming. No further series or seasons are yet believed to be greenlit.

items.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home's Mary Rivera, Ned's Grandma, Has Died Aged 82
items.description: Mary Rivera, the actress who played Ned's Grandma in Spider-Man: No Way Home, has died aged 82.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Mary Rivera, the actress who played Ned's Grandma in Spider-Man: No Way Home, has died aged 82.

While Rivera's contribution to Spider-Man: No Way Home was relatively short, her scene-stealing performance made her an instantly memorable addition to the movie's cast. And, even more impressively, this was despite the fact that the 2021 blockbuster was Rivera's only acting role.

Rivera's family previously revealed how they encouraged Mary to audition for the part after spotting a casting call advert posted to Facebook.

"I happened to be on a friend's Facebook scrolling," Rivera's daughter Kelly told Hawai'i Public Radio, "and I see an ad, a casting call looking for a local Hawai'i Filipina grandmother between the age of 50 and 90. And immediately I thought, 'Oh, well my mom qualifies and checks off all those boxes.'

"They just asked her to talk about herself and why she wanted to do the role. So she just gave a brief history of her time in the Philippines and what brought her to the United States, and raising her four children and 11 grandchildren — and basically that that is her biggest accomplishment of everything that she's done," Kelly added. "My mom has worn many hats over the years. She was a radio broadcaster, a teacher, but most notable was her role as a mother and grandmother."

Sadly, Rivera suffered a serious stroke in April and never recovered, TMZ has reported.

Jacob Batalon, who plays Ned in the Spider-Man franchise, has since offered his own message of condolence via Instagram, writing: "REST IN PARADISE LOLA😭❤️❤️❤️."

Five years on, Ned has returned in the just-released Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has already notched up nearly $1 billion at the box office. Perhaps the inevitable sequel will include a tribute to Rivera?

Image credit: Sony Pictures / YouTube

items.title: X-Men Fans Are Rediscovering That Samara Weaving Is a Huge Gamer After Emma Frost Casting
items.description: X-Men fans were more hyped than ever after Samara Weaving was cast as Emma Frost, but they got even more geeked after rediscovering that she’s a very serious gamer.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
X-Men fans were more hyped than ever after Samara Weaving was cast as Emma Frost, but they got even more geeked after discovering that she’s a very serious gamer.

Samara Weaving is your new Emma Frost. Beyond her astonishing resemblance to the glamorous mutant (that face card could not be more perfect for Emma), she’s also a loveable goofball and a massive gamer, something that came back to light once news of her casting hit the internet.

Back in March, Weaving spoke with IGN alongside fellow Ready or Not 2 star Kathryn Newton about their shared love for video games, revealing a wide variety of favorites that included Assassin’s Creed, Red Dead Redemption 2, Hogwarts Legacy, and even Mortal Kombat.

“I like an open world,” she told us, going on to say that her Mortal Kombat main is Kitana.

“I’m really good at it,” she said of the fighting game series. (Speaking of which, her friend, Jessica McNamee, plays Sonya Blade in the recent movies).

And in June 2026, Weaving gushed about her gaming habits in an episode of Polygon’s Shelf Quest, revealing that she hauls her PS5 with her everywhere she goes.

“All my jobs, I pack my PlayStation 5 in my suitcase, which is insane. It takes up half the suitcase and no one can lift it and they all hate me. But I bring it to every AirBnB and hotel that I stay at,” she told the outlet while standing among the crowded shelves of Videogamesnewyork.

In the interview, she revealed that her parents didn’t allow her to play video games growing up, saying she often played at friends’ houses when she could. She also reiterated her love of open world games, citing all the exploration and free-range roaming they allow.

But when it comes to fighting games, Weaving says they just ‘speak’ to her, saying she finds great success quite easily in both Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter.

“[Mortal Kombat] and Street Fighter, surprisingly, [I] was really good, really quick. I can beat a lot of people at Mortal Kombat. I don’t know why. It speaks to me, especially the chick with the fans — Kitana — I’m really good at Kitana. She’s my gal. She’s my fave.”

These interviews have sprung back up into the public consciousness, prompting no end of excitement and jokes as fans wait anxiously for more news on the X-Men reboot film.

“Imagine you’re getting your ass kicked by a Kitana, and it's her,” one wrote on X.

“She's rapidly climbing up the ladder of my fav actresses!” another said.

“Maybe she plays Marvel Rivals and plays Emma Frost,” yet another speculated.

While we can’t know that for certain just yet, we do have a few more details about the upcoming X-Men reboot film, directed by Jake Schreier. A number of other roles are currently undergoing casting, which reportedly began back in May, leaving fans even more hopeful for spot-on casting news in the near future.

With D23 set for August 14-16, there’s a good chance Marvel will reveal what it’s got up its sleeves, especially since it was so tight-lipped during its Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con in July.

Image Credits: Michael Tullberg/Getty Images / NetEase Games, Marvel Games

items.title: Kevin Feige Reveals Why Marvel Fought to Keep Sadie Sink's Role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day a Secret
items.description: Now that Spider-Man: Brand New Day has finally revealed Sadie Sink's mystery role, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has shared why the comic book movie company fought so hard to keep it a secret.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Now that Spider-Man: Brand New Day has finally revealed Sadie Sink's mystery role, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has shared why the comic book movie company fought so hard to keep it a secret.

Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow.

Sink plays… Jean Grey. Yes, fans, YouTube theorists, and just about everyone on the internet called it months ago, but that didn't stop Marvel Studios from playing its X-Men cards close to its chest for the new Tom Holland-led Spidey movie.

This version of comic book readers' treasured telepath was brought to the live-action world of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to play Spider-Man: Brand New Day's villain. She controls the minds of random New Yorkers, MJ (Zendaya), the Hulk (Mark Ruffalo), and the Punisher (Jon Bernthal), stops the city dead in its tracks, and tears apart the Department of Damage Control – but what was it all for?

Sink was cast in the movie all the way back in March 2025, with even reports at the time suggesting a part as Jean Grey was on the table. Marvel stayed tight-lipped regardless of all of the online chatter that followed, eventually going on to not only include a very quiet Sink in pre-release marketing but to start poking fun at the situation in the days leading up to the premiere.

After director Destin Daniel Cretton teased that Marvel had a "very real reason" to keep Sink's character's identity a secret, Feige finally broke his silence during a new interview with Variety. After more than a year of beating around the bush, his answer may leave you wanting more.

"It’s purely about creating the best possible opening weekend experience for the audience," Feige said.

According to him, it was all about the surprise. Marvel has, of course, kept major cameos and reveals a secret before, with Spider-Man: No Way Home being perhaps the most infamous example. When it comes to Sink as Jean Grey, though, the MCU puppeteer said there's a little more riding on what the X-Men character brings to the table than what she brought to just one movie.

"Sadie’s character is one that our fans know has immense significance within the Marvel Universe, and she plays a key role in the future of the MCU," he explained. "I’m just happy that the secret is finally out and that Sadie can stop dodging the question."

Sink hasn't had time to issue a public statement regarding her grand reveal, but that's probably because Spider-Man: Brand New Day is already tangling up headlines for other reasons. The new Spider-Man movie defied expectations by breaking records at the box office following its July 31 premiere. We're just now rounding out its fourth day in theaters, but after rounding up a whopping $930 million worldwide in its first weekend alone, it looks like $1 billion is just around the corner.

For more on the film, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review. You can also see what Sony Pictures executive Tom Rothman had to say about the anti-theater sentiment amongst some moviegoers, and what it would take to get Andrew Garfield back in costume.

Sink plays… Jean Grey. Yes, fans, YouTube theorists, and just about everyone on the internet called it months ago, but that didn't stop Marvel Studios from playing its X-Men cards close to its chest for the new Tom Holland-led Spidey movie.

This version of comic book readers' treasured telepath was brought to the live-action world of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to play Spider-Man: Brand New Day's villain. She controls the minds of random New Yorkers, MJ (Zendaya), the Hulk (Mark Ruffalo), and the Punisher (Jon Bernthal), stops the city dead in its tracks, and tears apart the Department of Damage Control – but what was it all for?

Sink was cast in the movie all the way back in March 2025, with even reports at the time suggesting a part as Jean Grey was on the table. After director Destin Daniel Cretton teased that Marvel had a "very real reason" to keep Sink's character's identity a secret, Feige finally broke his silence during a new interview with Variety. After more than a year of beating around the bush, his answer may leave you wanting more.

"It’s purely about creating the best possible opening weekend experience for the audience," Feige said.

According to him, it was all about the surprise. Marvel has, of course, kept major cameos and reveals a secret before, with Spider-Man: No Way Home being perhaps the most infamous example. When it comes to Sink as Jean Grey, though, the MCU puppeteer said there's a little more riding on what the X-Men character brings to the table than what she brought to just one movie.

"Sadie’s character is one that our fans know has immense significance within the Marvel Universe, and she plays a key role in the future of the MCU," he explained. "I’m just happy that the secret is finally out and that Sadie can stop dodging the question."

Sink hasn't had time to issue a public statement regarding her grand reveal, but that's probably because Spider-Man: Brand New Day is already tangling up headlines for other reasons. The new Spider-Man movie defied expectations by breaking records at the box office following its July 31 premiere. We're just now rounding out its fourth day in theaters, but after rounding up a whopping $930 million worldwide in its first weekend alone, it looks like $1 billion is just around the corner.

For more on the film, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review. You can also see what Sony Pictures executive Tom Rothman had to say about the anti-theater sentiment amongst some moviegoers, and what it would take to get Andrew Garfield back in costume.

items.title: Movie-Goers Evacuate Spider-Man: Brand New Day Screening After Viewer Lets 'Rotten' Fart Rip
items.description: An audience watching Spider-Man: Brand New Day was forced to flee after one movie-goer’s sour stomach turned the entire theater into a Dutch oven.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An audience watching Spider-Man: Brand New Day was forced to flee after one movie-goer’s sour stomach turned the entire theater into a Dutch oven.

The smelly situation happened on August 2 in Cartagena, Colombia, at the Cine Colombia multiplex inside the Plaza Bocagrande shopping center.

Reports state that halfway through the Marvel movie, one attendee just couldn’t hold it in anymore, releasing a “rotten” smell that was so foul it prompted security to evacuate the audience.

Despite the audience’s mass exodus, the theater didn’t pause or stop the screening, which continued until the credits rolled — but by that point, most Spidey fans had decided to leave and try their luck another day.

Footage from the incident quickly went viral on social media, showing stunned viewers pouring into a hallway outside the theater, one of whom was dressed in a Spider-Man costume calling someone on his phone, sparking no end of jokes online.

“The situation was so serious that Spiderman had to call in the Avengers,” one user joked online.

“The Green Goblin dropped a bomb,” another quipped.

“A great scent carries a great responsibility,” yet another riffed.

#MISERABLE 🤢 Una función de Spider-Man en el centro comercial Plaza Bocagrande, en Cartagena, terminó en anécdota insólita cuando un fuerte gas estomacal expulsado por un asistente obligó a varias personas a abandonar la sala de cine debido al insoportable mal olor. pic.twitter.com/UCpEQeAXrl

— Colombia Oscura (@ColombiaOscura) August 2, 2026

While reports speculate that a stink bomb prank could have been to blame, no culprits have yet been identified, leaving the smelly scenario shrouded in mystery. Staff say they have no idea who could have been behind the ordeal, either, and the theater itself has not issued a public statement on the matter.

Aside from this short-lived screening, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has enjoyed a record-breaking opening weekend at the box office, raking in $360 million domestically to beat out Avengers: Endgame’s previous record.

Globally, it still stands in second place to Endgame, earning $932 million at the worldwide box office in the year’s most profitable picture thus far. While the film didn’t initially release in IMAX, screenings are opening up on August 7, joining Nolan’s The Odyssey, the latter of which will continue to show in IMAX 70MM through mid-September.

In fact, Brand New Day is projected to blow past the $1 billion mark in the next few days, leaving Avengers: Doomsday with a lot more to live up to this December.

items.title: Sony's Spider-Man Spinoff Universe Might Be Dead as Company Confirms It Has No Movies in Active Development
items.description: It looks like Sony's Spider-Man spinoff universe may have come to an end after films like Madame Web, Morbius, and Kraven the Hunter failed to satisfy audiences.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
It looks like Sony's Spider-Man spinoff universe may have come to an end after films like Madame Web, Morbius, and Kraven the Hunter failed to satisfy audiences.

Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman confirmed its corner of Marvel moviemaking is currently without a plan during an interview with Variety. While the Venom trilogy starring Tom Hardy generally managed to find success at the box office, the critical and commercial reception for projects like Madame Web (2024) and Kraven the Hunter (2024) has the company reconsidering their future.

"Right now, we don’t know," Rothman said when asked if there are plans to expand on Sony's universe of Spider-Man characters. "We never looked at it as the 'Sony-Marvel Universe.' We looked at if there were worthwhile movies to make with other characters. At the moment, there are none in active development."

Rothman elaborated, saying that "the audience wasn't satisfied enough" with the live-action movies that filled out what many referred to as the "Sony-verse." Starting with Hardy's Venom in 2018, the full roster included that film, Venom: Let There Be Carnage, Morbius, Madame Web, Venom: The Last Dance, and Kraven the Hunter. Although Sony had, at one point, planned to integrate Spider-Man into the villain-led offshoots, such a crossover never came to fruition.

Kraven arrived as the final attempt to gain traction amongst comic book movie fans when it premiered in December 2024, but like many of the other Sony Spider-Man spinoffs, it failed to make an impact. Starring Marvel alum Aaron Taylor-Johnson, the film opened as the worst-performing entry in the Sony Marvel film series, with reviewers – including IGN – walking away less than impressed.

Despite the memes made along the way, it sounds like the poor performance has Sony rethinking how it uses these characters. Rothman's words today suggest his reboot teases from earlier this year might be on hold for a long while to come, if they materialize at all, after the movies failed to connect with audiences the first time around. At least there's still an animated Venom movie on the way.

"Whether that’s a fair assessment of those movies, who know," Rothman added, touching on the lack of impact on audiences. "That’s howling into the wind. The audience is the boss, and they didn’t respond. It’s as simple as that."

For now, the main Spider-Man universe is going strong. Spider-Man: Brand New Day just broke records in theaters, prompting Rothman to take a shot at the anti-theater sentiment that's driven conversations amongst moviegoers the last few years. For more, you can check out IGN's full breakdown for every Spider-Man universe movie in development.

items.title: Dave Bautista in Talks to Join God of War TV Series as Kratos
items.description: Dave Bautista is reportedly in talks to become Kratos in Prime Video's live-action God of War TV series.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Dave Bautista is reportedly in talks to become Kratos in Prime Video's live-action God of War TV series.

According to Variety and Deadline, Bautista has entered discussions to become PlayStation's beloved, brooding protagonist. The news comes just a few weeks after actor Ryan Hurst was dropped from the series after a bicep injury, which will require surgery. The production opted to recast Kratos as Hurst's injury means he won't be able to return to the series until sometime next year. If Bautista signs on, the plan is to get the show up and rolling again by the fall.

One advantage of Bautista provided by sources is that the actor is naturally already bulked up and wouldn't need months of training in order to get into the physique fans expect from Kratos. The actor is best known for his physical stature, having played Drax in the Guardians of the Galaxy films and hulking foes in films like Blade Runner 2049. He also has a history as a professional wrestler in the WWE, so he has the physical chops for it.

However, Bautista has lost a fair bit of weight/muscle in recent years. It's possible he's still ahead of the curve compared to most actors and could quickly put on the weight needed for Kratos, as Deadline states production won't begin until October. One other concern is that Bautista is 57 and would likely turn 58 during filming. Hurst was 50 when he got injured, meaning Bautista is just as likely, if not more, to be injured during the production of this show, especially across multiple seasons. Whether or not Amazon will put in more precautions to prevent that remains to be seen.

The actor previously campaigned to star in another adaptation of a franchise that has the GoW acronym: Gears of War. In 2018, he noted that Marcus Fenix was a "dream role" and that he'd actively been pursuing it with the rights holders. He later revealed that Universal, which was once developing Gears of War, wanted him to join the Fast and Furious franchise, but he turned it down in favor of pitching Gears of War. Now, Netflix is developing a Gears of War film, but it seems like PlayStation and Amazon may have beaten them to the punch.

Thanks to a report from MP1st, rumors also swirled over the weekend that the God of War TV series may be looking to recast Atreus actor Callum Vinson starting in season 2. It's believed this will allow the series to shoot quickly without having to wait for Vinson to grow up, as there is a three-year time jump between God of War 2018 and God of War Ragnarok, which will likely be the basis for season 2.

To top it all off, multiple new God of War games are also in the works. God of War Laufey is slated to release this coming February, while a new Kratos-led God of War game is also in development.

Photo by Mike Coppola/Getty Images

items.title: 'I Would Need It to Be Completely Unconventional' — Andrew Garfield Is Open to The Amazing Spider-Man 3 on One Condition
items.description: Andrew Garfield is open to coming back as Spidey for The Amazing Spider-Man 3, but it would need to be very weird.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Andrew Garfield is open to coming back as Spidey for The Amazing Spider-Man 3, but it would need to be very weird.

In an interview with The Playlist, Garfield was asked about his feelings toward returning as Peter Parker. The actor was hesitant to commit to anything, but said he would do another Spidey adventure if it were "strange" and "unconventional."

“I don’t know. I really don’t know,” Garfield said. “I would need it to be very, very odd. I would need it to be very strange, and I would need it to be completely unconventional and almost — I wouldn’t say boring — but I would want it to be just completely unexpected, like a genre of Spider-Man that you’ve never seen before, that feels very left field.”

So, what does that look like exactly? Garfield himself isn't totally sure, but he did throw out one possible idea that paints a picture of how outside the box he's thinking: “Maybe like a road trip movie," he suggested.

Andrew Garfield's run as Spider-Man ended prematurely back in 2014. The actor starred in The Amazing Spider-Man duology, which wasn't as beloved or commercially successful as Tobey Maguire's trilogy. After The Amazing Spider-Man 2 failed to meet Sony's expectations, it entered into conversations with Marvel Studios to integrate the webhead into the MCU. For a variety of reasons, the creative unit opted to drop Garfield and reboot everything, eventually selecting Tom Holland to be the next Spider-Man.

Holland has gone on to star in seven Marvel films as the wall-crawler and his latest, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, just had the biggest domestic opening weekend in history. It's expected that the film will cross the billion-dollar mark in its first four days and then barrel towards the $2 billion threshold.

Garfield did have an opportunity to reprise his role as Spider-Man and get some form of catharsis in Spider-Man: No Way Home. The film brought Tobey Maguire, Andrew Garfield, and Holland together in one big Spidey celebration. It allowed Garfield a form of redemption as the beloved character and even saw some reappraising his take. Ever since then, fans have been clamoring to see Garfield and Maguire return in new standalone films. It's unclear if that will ever happen, given Holland's take is thriving, but Maguire is rumored/heavily speculated to return in Avengers: Doomsday.

items.title: Sony Pictures CEO Jabs Anti-Theater Sentiment as Spider-Man: Brand New Day Breaks Box Office Records
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman on cloud nine, and he’s sticking it to folks who believe streaming will herald the death of the cinema experience.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman on cloud nine, and he’s sticking it to folks who believe streaming will herald the death of the cinema experience.

There’s something special about going to the movies; nothing really beats crunching on some salty, buttery popcorn, sitting in a nice, cushy chair, and watching a film on the big screen with booming surround sound while the worries of the outside world wait for two hours.

That’s the sentiment of Rothman, at least, following the record-breaking success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day at the box office this past weekend. Despite being a fairly standalone story compared to some of Peter Parker's previous big-screen adventures, it surpassed Avengers: Endgame to rake in $360 million domestically.

"So, I guess movies aren’t dead after all?" Rothman said in an interview with Variety’s Rebecca Rubin. "What happened is miraculous. Spider-Man is uniting people across cultures and ages. People can piss on theatrical all they want, but that’s one thing that only movies — and movie theaters — can do."

Brand New Day wasn’t just a box office hit at home; the latest Spidey flick also scored the second highest-grossing film debut globally at $932 million, coming in second to the eye-popping $1.223 billion earned by Avengers: Endgame back in April 2019.

Of course, given Brand New Day’s success, fans are equal parts certain of and eager to know if Tom Holland will return for another Spider-Man movie — something that Rothman couldn’t confirm for certain.

"I love these questions," he told the outlet. "It’s like when a coach wins the Super Bowl and he goes to the press conference and they say to him, 'Are you going to win it next year?' The honest truth is we don’t know at this point. This has been the focus of our studio for almost two years. I can tell you this: I certainly, certainly hope. I heard Tom say at some point that he wanted to continue, and we would love it if he did."

When Rubin pressed for more, asking if there’s a "world in which there will be another Spider-Man sequel with Tom Holland," Rothman simply answered, "Yes."

Back when No Way Home released in 2021, Holland said he hoped to play New York’s friendly neighborhood Spider-Man until he "can’t walk anymore," but more recently began speaking about taking on a successor when the time comes for him to put up the mask. Last week, he said details surrounding Spider-Man 5 were "unclear."

"For whoever’s next, whether that is a Miles Morales or a Spider-Gwen or a Spider-Woman or something like that, I would love to be a part of setting up the next chapter," he told Empire in May 2026. "Whatever that looks like, I don’t know. But if I could do what Downey did for me, then I would be so content swinging off into the sunset."

After also breaking Avengers: Endgame's records for domestic previews and opening days, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is still going strong, and will even receive IMAX screenings starting August 7, joining the The Odyssey as Nolan's epic adpatation extends its IMAX 70MM offerings to mid-September.

The honest truth is we don’t know at this point. This has been the focus of our studio for almost two years. I can tell you this: I certainly, certainly hope. I heard Tom say at some point that he wanted to continue, and we would love it if he did."

When Rubin pressed for more, asking if there’s a "world in which there will be another Spider-Man sequel with Tom Holland," Rothman simply answered, "Yes."

Back when No Way Home released in 2021, Holland said he hoped to play New York’s friendly neighborhood Spider-Man until he "can’t walk anymore," but more recently began speaking about taking on a successor when the time comes for him to put up the mask. Last week, he said details surrounding Spider-Man 5 were "unclear."

"For whoever’s next, whether that is a Miles Morales or a Spider-Gwen or a Spider-Woman or something like that, I would love to be a part of setting up the next chapter," he told Empire in May 2026. "Whatever that looks like, I don’t know. But if I could do what Downey did for me, then I would be so content swinging off into the sunset."

After also breaking Avengers: Endgame's records for domestic previews and opening days, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is still going strong, and will even receive IMAX screenings starting August 7, joining the The Odyssey as Nolan's epic adpatation extends its IMAX 70MM offerings to mid-September.

items.title: The Steam Frame Might End Up More Expensive Than the Steam Machine
items.description: In a now-deleted stream, Valve leaker Tyler McVicker suggests the Steam Frame could be more expensive than the Steam Machine.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The Steam Machine launched a little over a month ago, and it came with quite a controversial price tag. But it seems like the Steam Frame might end up even more expensive than Valve's mini gaming PC.

According to a now-deleted Stream by Valve leaker Tyler Mcvicker, and spotted by NotebookCheck, the Steam Frame could end up at a price at or above $1,100. The deleted stream also apparently suggested the VR headset would come out as early as today, so I'd take all of this with a massive grain of salt. But even if I wouldn't necessarily put a lot of stock in the actual number reported by McVicker, it's entirely possible that the Steam Frame is going to be much more expensive than the Steam Machine, and that's due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

The Steam Frame is going to be equipped with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 SoC with 16GB of memory and either 256GB or 1TB of UFS (universal flash storage). Even though the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 is a couple years old at this point, it's still a relatively powerful mobile processor. And it's being paired with 16GB of DDR5, and we all know how that went for the Steam Machine. It doesn't help that the Steam Frame has design considerations that the Steam Machine just didn't have to deal with.

Each eye will have a 2160x2160 LCD display with a 144Hz refresh rate, and there are a total of six cameras strapped onto the headset, to track head and eye movement when you're playing games. Plus, Valve engineered an impressive wireless transmission method, that can intelligently render games based on what you're looking at.

So, even if the Steam Frame struggles to run a lot of games locally – which Valve's engineers basically told us it would back in October – there's a lot more than just a GPU and some RAM to consider. It's important to keep in mind, too, that the Valve Index was quite expensive for its time, costing a whopping $999 when it came out in 2019. So, it's not that much of a stretch to imagine that the Frame will be even more expensive whenever it eventually comes out.

At the end of the day, no one will know exactly how much the Steam Frame is going to cost until Valve actually launches the thing. However, the Steam Machine did come out roughly 7 weeks after the Steam Controller launched on May 4. If Valve keeps up that same timing, we could see the new VR headset's Steam page open up as early as August 10.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Shift Up CEO Defends Stellar Blade: Blood Rain AI Music Video Against Player Backlash
items.description: The CEO of Shift Up has responded to backlash surrounding the release of an AI-generated music video promoting Stellar Blade’s sequel game, Blood Rain.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The CEO of Shift Up has responded to backlash surrounding the release of an AI-generated music video promoting Stellar Blade’s sequel game, Blood Rain.

The video, published on July 31, showed the game’s main character, Evie, singing and dancing to an upbeat pop song titled "Wanna be in Love." It’s very obviously AI-generated, containing all the signature tells of such content, including nonsensical written wording, inconsistencies in character models, and a blurred, airbrushed filter over it all.

This has soured players on the otherwise highly-anticipated title, prompting a harsh wave of criticism that warranted a response from developer Shift Up’s CEO, Kim Hyung Tae.

"Wanna be in LOVE" feat. EVIE from Stellar Blade : BLOODRAIN
EVIE’s new music video is now available in YouTube. I would be very grateful if you could watch the video and share your thoughts! https://t.co/n1bhFiH1IJ#StellarBlade #BLOODRAIN #EVIE pic.twitter.com/eNiLyZAQ5W

— Kim Hyung Tae, 김형태, キム・ヒョンテ (@jamm3rd) July 31, 2026

Speaking on X (formerly Twitter), Kim praised the artists responsible for the design of the game’s main character, Evie, arguing that an AI merely used their work to compile the scenes showing her dancing and singing rather than making anything on its own from scratch.

“EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work. The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and craftsmanship our team created. We would truly appreciate it if you could view the work with that understanding in mind,” he wrote.

Unsurprisingly, this explanation didn’t put players’ minds at ease. If anything, it left them even more frustrated and somewhat confused, with some pointing out that training an AI model on the designs of Shift Up’s designers does them a disservice and even bastardizes the artistry behind all their hard work.

EVIE, the character at the heart of this video, was created from head to toe by our talented artists and modelers through more than a year of dedicated work.

The AI is not creating her from scratch. It is rendering and presenting the character based on the data, designs, and…

— Kim Hyung Tae, 김형태, キム・ヒョンテ (@jamm3rd) July 31, 2026

“The AI is doing your character a disservice, distorting her appearance, and in turn, making your team's art look bad, when in reality, they're so talented,” one fan wrote on X. “I would rather have fewer, shorter cinematics of your characters made by animators than hours of uncanny AI generations.”

“That’s the issue though, it does not look like her a lot of the time, even if they might use the base model as part of the input. You're diminishing the quality of your own work, the brand, the studio, and Evie as a character,” another argued.

“You also risk associating the brand with AI slop, even if that might be true or not. You risk being in a position where the game might have some amazing set pieces or city backdrops that designers and developers made, and people will dismiss it as AI-generated.”

It’s worth noting that this is merely a music video promoting Stellar Blade: Blood Rain and not the game itself. However, Kim has previously remarked on AI in reference to Korea’s competition with China in the gaming space, claiming Shift Up doesn’t have the manpower to compete with Chinese studios.

"80% of our company's revenue comes from overseas, and when we go abroad, the first opponent we encounter is Chinese games. We pour about 150 people into a single game, but China invests 1,000 to 2,000. We lack the capability to compete in terms of the quality or quantity of content,” he said back in January, per GameMeca.

"I do not think people will lose their jobs even if AI becomes widespread. Even if we mobilize all available manpower, it will not be enough, and I believe that we can only barely compete with industries like China or the United States that require massive workforce deployments if all these people are proficient in AI and one person can perform the role of 100."

What’s more, Kim predicted a future where AI is central to the games industry, pointing out how quickly young people are picking it up as an essential tool in daily life.

"(Korea's) ChatGPT paid subscription rate ranks second after the United States. The new generation is natural to AI. I believe that AI is the future of the younger generation and can become a new vision applicable to industry."

The Stellar Blade games themselves are no stranger to controversy, with Kim most recently addressing the debate that cropped up around Evie’s youthful design following Blood Rain’s reveal at Summer Game Fest. Given how sexualized Eve was in Stellar Blade, players were worried about how Evie might be perceived by some fans.

Speaking with IGN, the Shift Up CEO promised that “if you actually play the game, you will not think that,” telling us that, when combined with her scrappy nature and other features, players will “see that she’s a very lovable character.”

items.title: Microsoft Reportedly Working to Bring Xbox 360 Games to PC and Project Helix
items.description: Microsoft reportedly has plans to allow developers to bring their Xbox 360 games to PC, as well as other Xbox devices.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Microsoft reportedly has plans to allow developers to bring their Xbox 360 games to PC, as well as other Xbox devices.

That's according to a leaked document sent to Microsoft's partners that was seen by The Verge. What appeared to be a portion of the document showing a roadmap for features set to come in the coming months and years also leaked over the weekend.

it looks like devs won’t have to do any engineering work to get Xbox 360 and Xbox games on PC. Microsoft’s Xbox PC emulator handles it all 👍 https://t.co/3veMXdaJb2 pic.twitter.com/daFEomcVUa

— Tom Warren (@tomwarren) August 3, 2026

The alleged plan is to allow players to play classic Xbox 360 titles not only on "Xbox PCs," but the upcoming Project Helix device and handheld hardware, as well. Microsoft previously announced a similar strategy in July, though backward compatibility on that front was limited to original Xbox games.

The report added that developers will have the freedom to bring their Xbox 360 games to the aforementioned devices – but the feature won't officially launch for some time. Potentially eligible titles aren't expected to begin their gradual rollout on next-gen Xbox hardware until sometime between 2027 and 2028. At that point, the expectation is reportedly that developers will be able to make their games backward compatible. They will also maintain control over pricing and Game Pass availability.

Original Xbox games were set to begin disc-to-digital testing for insiders last month, with availability for all coming this month. The Verge reported that the beta was delayed, so when that's still in the cards for is unclear.

The Verge reported early last month that Microsoft was exploring ways for players to digitally transfer their physical games. Today's report added some clarity to that, stating that physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X games placed in console disc drives will grant players a digital license that is bound to "that disc and the player's account." However, should a disc be traded with someone else, digital ownership can be swapped to that person.

In other words, should this strategy pan out, trading eligible Xbox discs will work similarly to how it has before we started careening toward an all-digital future. It's unclear if it's a solution that will be celebrated by players who have fought for physical media to stay.

The conversation surrounding how gaming company's are slowely doing away with physical media has heated up in recent months. Rockstar Games sparked fears online when it announced Grand Theft Auto 6 would launch with a code in its box instead of a disc. Those fears were then realized when Sony declared it would cease production for physical games starting in January 2028, a decision it's still feeling the reprecussions of.

How Microsoft will fit into an increasingly heavy digital gaming landscape remains to be seen, but it wouldn't be a surprise to see it do away with physical releases, too. While we wait to see how the future will pan out, you can see how Sony responded to the backlash last week. You can also read up on the Xbox console price increases that swept across Europe over the weekend.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.title: Rockstar Games Killed Midnight Club 5 Because It Wasn't as Big as GTA, Ex-Designer Claims
items.description: An ex-Rockstar Games designer claims that the studio killed the Midnight Club franchise as it wasn't as big as Grand Theft Auto.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
An ex-Rockstar Games designer claims that the studio killed the Midnight Club franchise as it wasn't as big as Grand Theft Auto.

In an interview with Insider Gaming, former Rockstar senior designer Kris Roberts was asked about Midnight Club's fate, having worked on the franchise at Rockstar San Diego — the studio that helmed Rockstar's arcade racing franchise and led development on the first Red Dead Redemption. Roberts noted that a fifth Midnight Club game was in early development following the release of Midnight Club: Los Angeles and the team had even prototyped new locations, including London.

Unfortunately, the plug was pulled on the racing game during its development phase. Roberts noted that there was a "non-trivial conflict" between Rockstar San Diego and the more central Rockstar New York. The designer noted that while there had been legitimate frustrations over missed deadlines on the previous Midnight Club game, Rockstar still hadn't given the racing series its props as it wasn't nearly as big as GTA.

“The perception was we never got the accolades or the reception,” Roberts explained. “The New York perspective was, ‘You’re not GTA’. When you’re the red-headed stepchild project — you know, we’re doing a good job, we’re world-class, but we’re still treated less than. It was challenging.”

Roberts also stated that Midnight Club kept players more engaged than competitors like Need for Speed and Burnout, but it wasn't enough. Unfortunately, the cancelation of Midnight Club 5 signaled to a lot of people that the franchise was unlikely to return and as a result, remaining staff moved on to work on Red Dead Redemption or other projects within Rockstar.

“When they cancelled it, it was pretty clear that there would be no more Midnight Club and everything was going to be GTA and stuff moving forward, and that’s just the way it was going to be," said Roberts.

One of the big complaints from fans is that Rockstar hasn't diversified enough since Grand Theft Auto 5. A sequel to Red Dead Redemption made sense as the studio's follow up, but it has now meant that Rockstar has been in a loop of GTA and Red Dead games for a decade and a half. Some fans fear this is the future of Rockstar and that we won't get more unique, smaller-scale games like Bully, LA Noire, or Midnight Club anymore.

Rockstar will have the opportunity to do whatever it wants after GTA 6, given it will make unfathomable amounts of money. The studio is publishing a pair of Max Payne remakes, developed by Remedy, but it's unclear when these will see the light of day. Whether or not Rockstar will revisit any of these dormant franchises itself or try something new after GTA 6 remains to be seen.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

“The perception was we never got the accolades or the reception,” Roberts explained. “The New York perspective was, ‘You’re not GTA’. When you’re the red-headed stepchild project — you know, we’re doing a good job, we’re world-class, but we’re still treated less than. It was challenging.”

Roberts also stated that Midnight Club kept players more engaged than competitors like Need for Speed and Burnout, but it wasn't enough. Unfortunately, the cancelation of Midnight Club 5 signaled to a lot of people that the franchise was unlikely to return and as a result, remaining staff moved on to work on Red Dead Redemption or other projects within Rockstar.

“When they cancelled it, it was pretty clear that there would be no more Midnight Club and everything was going to be GTA and stuff moving forward, and that’s just the way it was going to be," said Roberts.

One of the big complaints from fans is that Rockstar hasn't diversified enough since Grand Theft Auto 5. A sequel to Red Dead Redemption made sense as the studio's follow up, but it has now meant that Rockstar has been in a loop of GTA and Red Dead games for a decade and a half. Some fans fear this is the future of Rockstar and that we won't get more unique, smaller-scale games like Bully, LA Noire, or Midnight Club anymore.

Rockstar will have the opportunity to do whatever it wants after GTA 6, given it will make unfathomable amounts of money. The studio is publishing a pair of Max Payne remakes, developed by Remedy, but it's unclear when these will see the light of day. Whether or not Rockstar will revisit any of these dormant franchises itself or try something new after GTA 6 remains to be seen.

items.title: 'To Be Able to Identify the Mechanism Does Not Invalidate the Mechanism' — Christopher Nolan Lays Out a 'Fundamental Flaw' With Amateur Film Criticism
items.description: Christopher Nolan has laid out what he believes to be a "fundamental flaw" with amateur film criticism.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Christopher Nolan has laid out what he believes to be a "fundamental flaw" with amateur film criticism.

The director in charge of July box office hit The Odyssey examined how audiences pick apart movies during an interview with podcast host Zhong Shu. He took aim at those who recognize the inner workings of how a movie chooses to tell its story and then spin that as if it's a negative.

He explained, "To identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism."

"I think that, when you're talking about storytelling, you're always in conversation with the expectations of the audience," Nolan said. "So it really is an energy that's brought from the audience, as well as an energy that's put forward from the story itself.

"The trite version of this, or the criticism often leveled at movies in general, is, 'Oh, the character has to be made sympathetic, so the character is manipulated in different ways and changed in different ways.' That's a fundamental flaw of film criticism in a way, or storytelling criticism, because to be able to identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism.

"That's a real problem with criticism today because people have this idea that, 'Because I can understand why the story affects me the way it is, therefore, it didn't work.' That's not how storytelling works."

He continued, saying that, when storytellers create their heroic figures, they must be "mindful of the energy that the audience brings to that story and the interaction between our intention and the way the audience receives that."

Nolan opened the door for critics to pick apart his latest project when The Odyssey set sail in theaters, including Imax, last month. Although the negative noise surrounding it actually quietened down a bit upon its release, there are those who have been quite vocal when it comes to their problems with the film.

One notable individual to have spoken up included Greek translator Emily Wilson, who Nolan had previously cited during the lead-up to The Odyssey's premiere. She published a harsh (and lengthy) review of the movie last week, saying she would have been "ashamed to have written any part of this script."

As Nolan elaborated on his thoughts, he made it clear that his complaint with how some approach film criticism is not directed at professional critics, but amateur ones.

"When I was talking about film criticism, I was talking more about amateur film criticism than professional film criticism because professional film criticism tends to understand the necessity for the mechanisms. So, you're looking at a lingua franca of storytelling created by Hollywood for the last hundred years that is very, effectively universal.

"So, it is its own language, and that language is understood by people all over the world, which is what's incredible about it. It is a very accessible, modern language of storytelling, and it has certain rules. It has conventions. You can break those conventions. You can bend them. You can move them, but you have to be aware of them the whole time.

Here is my interview with Christopher Nolan: are you a bard for a civilization at dusk? pic.twitter.com/dQION5v6bl

— Yiyang Zhuge (@ZhugeYY) July 31, 2026

"As I say, I'm thinking more of amateur criticism when I say that people who, because they feel they've identified the mechanism, they feel that it invalidates it, that can be true of certain elements, and film grammar – film language – evolves with that. So, when a trope becomes too familiar to an audience, then it has to be changed, but we do, as filmmakers, avail ourselves of that common language. We build on that understanding. Our audience has seen many films, and they understand that language, and so you're playing with that language."

Nolan is no stranger to criticism online. Conversations about The Odyssey have been polluted by complaints regarding a lack of "historical accuracy" and its casting choices. The director has said he wasn't too bothered by it, though, especially when it came to the backlash that arrived before the film even premiered.

He told The Telegraph that the conversations that happen before a film's arrival are "always irrelevant." He also added that his 10 years of work with Batman helped him prepare for some of the more vocal moviegoers.

When it comes to The Odyssey's journey post-release, however, it seems the cast and crew backing the film have little to worry about. As relayed by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, critics and audiences have largely fallen in love with the film. We here at IGN gave it an 8/10 review.

The movie recently had its 70mm Imax release extended by one month after it exceeded expectations at the box office during its July 17 opening weekend. Following weekends have been similarly successful, as its second dropped just 19%, while its third saw it cross $900 million globally as it continues the trek to $1 billion.

Photo by Han Myung-Gu/WireImage.

items.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Update 1.0.6 Launches Tomorrow — Here Are the Patch Notes
items.description: Ubisoft has announced an update for Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced will land tomorrow, August 4.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Ubisoft has announced an update for Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced will land tomorrow, August 4.

Update 1.0.6 will become available to download on PC and consoles from 7am Pacific / 10am Eastern / 3pm UK time, and weigh in at 15.2GB on Xbox Series X/S, 5.03GB on PlayStation 5, or 1.8GB on Steam.

While Ubisoft seems keen to support its hugely popular Black Flag remake for the time being (and yes, that does include the addition of a New Game Plus mode), it is still early days. So, don't expect big things from this particular update.

Indeed, the largest change that players will probably notice is the ability to now hide Edward Kenway's blowpipe, which rather sticks out on his back at the moment. With Update 1.0.6 installed, you'll be able to hit R2 to "Hide Gear" when selecting your outfit in the inventory screen. This will let you toggle the blowpipe on or off to match your fit.

Other than that, the rest of this patch's changes are listed as bug fixes, though there's some interesting issues listed. Did you know there was supposed to be a tutorial for throwing money? Its absence was a glitch that has now been sorted.

Also, did you spot that the Kraken ship wheel was listed as far too pricey for you to initially buy? "Fixed an issue where the Kraken wheel cost was listed incorrectly," Ubisoft's patch notes confirm, noting that "the Kraken wheel is wheely expensive."

Tomorrow's full patch notes lie below for your perusal:

PATCH 1.0.6 HIGHLIGHTS:

The Blowpipe Can Now Be Hidden: We saw your feedback, and we have given players the option to hide the “Blow Pipe” from Edward’s back. In order to do so, access your outfit in the inventory and select R2 for the option to “Hide Gear”. Or “Show Gear” if you’d prefer the “Blow Pipe” be visible on certain outfits.

List of Bug Fixes

General

  • Increased number of autosaves from 5 to 10 to allow players to load from earlier progressions.
  • Fixed an issue on PC where Cutscenes could be locked at 30 FPS when Graphics settings were set to ‘custom’ from any ‘Low’ presets.
  • Added missing tutorial on how to ‘Throw Money’.
  • Fixed an issue where DLC Pack notifications could appear at the start of a new game.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward could start sliding right after fast travelling to a synchronized viewpoint while sprinting and jumping down.
  • Fixed an issue on PC for Mouse & Keyboard where Quest icon could be marked/unmarked when selecting the Quest tab.
  • Fixed an issue where players did not receive a purchase confirmation message for Resource Packs.
  • Fixed an issue where players could be unable to parkour while holding down RT after remapping RT to sprint.
  • Fixed minor crashes that could happen during Ground and Naval fights.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward’s hood could not be toggled during the Leap of Faith.

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where players could be unable to perform leg sweeps on enemies in an ‘attentive’ or ‘suspicious’ state.
  • Fixed an issue where the Brute Elites were sometimes not charging towards the player.
  • Fixed an issue that could occur when players tried to hire dancers while on top of a box.
  • Fixed an issue where “Quick Use Rope Dart” may no longer be usable when interrupted by an enemy attack or after a rope dart hang.
  • Fixed an issue where players were sometimes unable to assassinate drunk pirates in smoke after entering combat with them.
  • Fixed an issue where Enemy ships sometimes did no damage when ramming the Jackdaw at certain angles.
  • Fixed an issue where dead bodies on benches could be looted/carried after loading a save file.
  • Fixed delayed reaction from guards upon seeing a hanging dead body.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward wasn’t always turning to look at where he was aiming in a Naval battle.
  • Fixed an issue where Edward could trigger a takedown while vaulting over the enemy.
  • Fixed an issue where the Naval Convoy’s leader could go flying after lowering wanted level or sending it to Kenway’s fleet during Boarding.

World

  • Fixed an issue where players may get stuck when attempting to parkour between a tree and a wall in Kingston.
  • Fixed an issue where players could ‘Fast Travel’ to an unsynchronized viewpoint in Havana.
  • Fixed an issue where there was no warning message displayed when trying to fast travel to a captured fort while in a restricted area.
  • Fixed an issue where players could get stuck in free fall when climbing behind the chest at Mariguana Island.

Progression & Economy

  • Fixed an issue where the Kraken wheel cost was listed incorrectly / the Kraken wheel is wheely expensive.
  • Fixed an issue where ‘The Benjamin’ ship codex unlocked at a later quest.

UI/Menu

  • Updated font for Simplified Chinese to allow for better readability.
  • Fixed an issue where players may become soft-locked when switching to the Map tab while visualizing a Codex entry.
  • Fixed alignment issues when language was set to Arabic.
  • Fixed an issue where Ally ship icons were displayed
  • Fixed an issue where the Vision Preset’s enabled black background for objectives remained on during Modern Rifts.

Visuals & Graphics

  • Fixed multiple animation issues.
  • Fixed minor ragdoll issues.
  • Fixed multiple camera issues during assassinations.
  • Fixed lighting issues while underwater.
  • Fixed visual gaps present in the Fort wall of Nassau.
  • Fixed Enemies’ blood coming out from hips instead of chin during the pistol finishing kill
  • Fixed visual issues in Tavern Brawl with knocking out enemies near tables and chairs.
  • Fixed clipping issues with the cape of ‘Hellion Armor’ when there are strong winds.
  • Fixed issues where PSSR was not properly enabled if the same account was used first on PS5 and then on PS5 Pro

Localization

  • Fixed incorrect localization of “Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced” on all platform packages in Simplified Chinese.
  • Fixed incorrect localization of the Trophy/Achievement “Ed the Diver” in Simplified Chinese.

Audio

  • Fixed various missing audio issues.
  • Fixed missing audio for when a normal guard blocked melee attacks from the player.
  • Fixed an issue where the Hideout’s watermill audio would be played after entering and exiting the menu despite the Hideout’s Garden not being unlocked.
  • Balanced certain dialogues in Simplified Chinese to be more audible.

SPOILERS AHEAD!

Quests

  • "Overrun and Outnumbered": Fixed an issue where James Kidd remained idle if the player skipped the cutscene and quickly used a “Sleep Dart” on an enemy.
  • “Delirium”: Fixed an issue where the sails could be seen floating when swimming up.
  • “Traveling Salesman”: Fixed an issue where low-quality civilian models could be observed if the player skipped through the cutscene.
  • “Vainglorious Bastards”: Fixed an issue where the “Royal African Ship” could sometimes sink after the cutscene.
  • “A Second Chance”: Fixed an issue where Edward could fast travel to the Jackdaw while carrying food, which may cause the food to disappear.
  • “Mayan Mysteries”: Fixed an issue where the “Mayan Armor” could not be obtained due to missing a Mayan stone that was obtained before “Overrun and Outnumbered” quest.
  • “A Cockalorum”: Lucy will sometimes go out of hiding during 'Reach the villa' objective.
  • “The Sage's buried secret”: Fixed an issue where James Kidd could get stuck if the player blocks his route up the rocks.
  • “What the Devil!”: Fixed an issue where players could unintentionally clear the objective “Board the HMS Demolition” as Edward.
  • “Templar Ships”: Fixed an issue where players could remain stuck in combat if they were detected by enemies while eavesdropping on civilians.
  • “Upton Travers”: Fixed an issue where the objective to ‘Kill Upton’ was missing after loading a save file.
  • “Diving for Medicines”: Fixed an issue where players could lose autosave files if they participate in “Uptown Travers” during the main quest.
  • Fixed an issue in certain quests where enemies did not react accordingly if inflicted by sleep/berserk dart while following another person.
  • Fixed an issue where on Black Island, "Morgan's Treasures" and "Midnight Moonshine" could sometimes remain unavailable to players.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Avengers: Doomsday's Chances of an IMAX Release Just Got More Likely
items.description: An Avengers: Doomsday IMAX release doesn't seem totally out of the question anymore.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
An Avengers: Doomsday IMAX release doesn't seem totally out of the question anymore.

Earlier today, it was announced that Spider-Man: Brand New Day will be hitting IMAX screens in North America later this week. This came as a bit of a surprise to fans, as the film wasn't marketed for the format and instead opted to use other premium large format screens such as ScreenX, 4DX, and Dolby. However, Brand New Day was shot with IMAX in mind and certain sequences were filmed for the format's aspect ratio, according to director Destin Daniel Cretton.

Ultimately, it seems like Sony was aware it wanted an IMAX release a while ago, but kept it under wraps, possibly to encourage fans to see it again. That strategy will likely generate further profits for Marvel as the film has already made nearly a billion dollars in its opening weekend alone and enthusiastic fans are looking to see it second time — now with an added reason to go.

With that said, Marvel has already confirmed that Avengers: Doomsday will not release in IMAX when it hits theaters on December 18th. The situation is similar to Spider-Man, which released in The Odyssey's three-week exclusivity window on IMAX screens. Doomsday will be hitting theaters the same day as Dune Part 3, which will have its own exclusivity on IMAX screens. The window has yet to be confirmed, but it will likely be two or three weeks, ensuring the sci-fi trilogy capper dominates screens throughout the end of 2026.

But once that window is up, it wouldn't be surprising if Disney pounces. It would give Avengers: Doomsday a second wind, especially as January is a notoriously quiet month for major movie releases. IMAX has only become more and more prominent as time has gone on, especially after The Odyssey's highly successful run, and it's a format that fans are enamored by. It would likely drive a healthy amount of people to IMAX theaters to either see the film for the first time if they prioritized Dune in December or see it again.

Currently, there's no word on whether or not Avengers: Doomsday was shot with IMAX in mind and Marvel probably won't reveal that until it's ready to show its cards. Indeed, in the meantime, Marvel has been marketing a new theatrical branding known as "Infinity Vision." While some thought this was a brand new format, it's actually a certification from Disney that a theater meets a certain level of quality. Admittedly, the standards are low and the movie doesn't even need to be shown on a premium format in order to be qualify.

IMAX CEO Rich Gilfond was previously very dismissive of Infinity Vision, noting that it's just a marketing tactic to make up for the lack of IMAX screens.

"It's not a new technological advance in any way; it's a marketing initiative, because Disney could not play Avengers in IMAX because we had committed to Dune 3," Gilfond said. "Disney really wanted to figure out a way that they could market to audiences. So they created this initiative. It's not going to open an additional projection system. It's not going to add any special look or feel to the film. It is a way to market Avengers. We'll find out if it works or not."

Some speculated that these comments and behind the scenes disputes may have created a tense relationship between Marvel and IMAX, but Spider-Man and the upcoming re-release of Avengers: Endgame both getting the IMAX treatment may suggest it's not that bad. After all, Marvel is a cash cow, and it would also benefit IMAX to milk it if it gets the opportunity.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

An Avengers: Doomsday IMAX release doesn't seem totally out of the question anymore.

Earlier today, it was announced that Spider-Man: Brand New Day will be hitting IMAX screens in North America later this week. This came as a bit of a surprise to fans, as the film wasn't marketed for the format and instead opted to use other premium large format screens such as ScreenX, 4DX, and Dolby. However, Brand New Day was shot with IMAX in mind and certain sequences were filmed for the format's aspect ratio, according to director Destin Daniel Cretton.

Ultimately, it seems like Sony was aware it wanted an IMAX release a while ago, but kept it under wraps, possibly to encourage fans to see it again. That strategy will likely generate further profits for Marvel as the film has already made nearly a billion dollars in its opening weekend alone and enthusiastic fans are looking to see it second time — now with an added reason to go.

With that said, Marvel has already confirmed that Avengers: Doomsday will not release in IMAX when it hits theaters on December 18th. The situation is similar to Spider-Man, which released in The Odyssey's three-week exclusivity window on IMAX screens. Doomsday will be hitting theaters the same day as Dune Part 3, which will have its own exclusivity on IMAX screens. The window has yet to be confirmed, but it will likely be two or three weeks, ensuring the sci-fi trilogy capper dominates screens throughout the end of 2026.

But once that window is up, it wouldn't be surprising if Disney pounces. It would give Avengers: Doomsday a second wind, especially as January is a notoriously quiet month for major movie releases. IMAX has only become more and more prominent as time has gone on, especially after The Odyssey's highly successful run, and it's a format that fans are enamored by. It would likely drive a healthy amount of people to IMAX theaters to either see the film for the first time if they prioritized Dune in December or see it again.

Currently, there's no word on whether or not Avengers: Doomsday was shot with IMAX in mind and Marvel probably won't reveal that until it's ready to show its cards. Indeed, in the meantime, Marvel has been marketing a new theatrical branding known as "Infinity Vision." While some thought this was a brand new format, it's actually a certification from Disney that a theater meets a certain level of quality. Admittedly, the standards are low and the movie doesn't even need to be shown on a premium format in order to be qualify.

IMAX CEO Rich Gilfond was previously very dismissive of Infinity Vision, noting that it's just a marketing tactic to make up for the lack of IMAX screens.

"It's not a new technological advance in any way; it's a marketing initiative, because Disney could not play Avengers in IMAX because we had committed to Dune 3," Gilfond said. "Disney really wanted to figure out a way that they could market to audiences. So they created this initiative. It's not going to open an additional projection system. It's not going to add any special look or feel to the film. It is a way to market Avengers. We'll find out if it works or not."

Some speculated that these comments and behind the scenes disputes may have created a tense relationship between Marvel and IMAX, but Spider-Man and the upcoming re-release of Avengers: Endgame both getting the IMAX treatment may suggest it's not that bad. After all, Marvel is a cash cow, and it would also benefit IMAX to milk it if it gets the opportunity.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Pokémon Go's LEGO Store Promotion is Now Live — Here's Where to Find a Location Near You
items.description: Pokémon Go's LEGO collaboration is now live, bringing exclusive in-game rewards if you stop by a participating store — so, here's where to find one.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pokémon Go's LEGO collaboration is now live, bringing exclusive in-game rewards if you stop by a participating store — so, here's where to find one.

LEGO and Pokémon Go have teamed up this year as the former rolls out a range of Pokémon LEGO sets, many of which are infused with Smart Play technology. Pokémon Go also celebrated the European leg of its big summer events in Copenhagen, just a stone's throw from LEGO's global headquarters, and rolled out exclusive in-game bonuses.

Well, those in-game bonuses have thankfully become a lot easier to obtain for other Pokémon Go players, as long as you live in the U.S., Europe or Australia. Select LEGO stores across these regions now host all-day raids and sponsored PokéStops, which all bestow special goodies.

So, what do you get? Well, every day, each location will host one all-day raid that awards a Pikachu with a LEGO special background. Spinning the sponsored stops, meanwhile, will award LEGO Pokémon in-game stickers. Of course, you don't physically need to go into a LEGO store to get these bonuses, as you can interact with the in-game locations just by standing near. Indeed, head close enough and you'll also unlock an in-game Stamp Rally, which awards another Pikachu and records your progress if you visit further LEGO store locations.

With just over 200 participating stores, there's too many to list out here in full. However, an interactive map right here will now show you where to find the location closest to you.

In the U.S., the majority of states have at least one participating LEGO store. Over in Europe, the UK has around 20 — including four in London. And in mainland Europe, France, Germany and Poland also have local stores — though, strangely, there are none in Denmark.

This summer, Pokémon Go is celebrating its 10th year of operation (yes, it really has been a decade since it all began). Up next for the game will be its big end of summer Go Fest Finale event, where players expect more Mega Pokémon to make their debut, alongside other surprises. LEGO, meanwhile, has a fresh wave of Pokémon sets coming on October 1, including the $299.99 Iconic Trainer Moments: Poké Ball set, which will contain the first LEGO Pokémon minifigures.

Image credit: LEGO
